One of my favorite bits of trivia is about Newman and, while it is a favorite, it’s also rather grim.

When James Dean died in a car accident in 1955, he had finished *Giant* and was signed on to play in two films which, obviously, he was unable to do.

Both films were eventually made and both of them featured very early roles for, you guessed it, Paul Newman.

*The Left Handed Gun* (1958) is mostly forgotten today and considered mediocre.  It featured Paul Newman doing his best James Dean in a Billy the Kid western.

However, *Somebody Up There Likes Me* (1956), the biopic of boxer Rocky Graziano, was both a critical and commercial hit and may well have helped propel Newman into being considered a bankable “star”.

Thus, and again it’s a grim thing to think about, but James Dean’s passing in a way helped Paul Newman… at least in the short term.
Or Ray Scheider, for that matter!
